sheet.howExamined: Unit 3 is one 1-hour calculator paper of 50 marks, sat every Summer. The standard deviation of a raw list is set as a part of 3 to 5 marks: Summer 2025 Q2 was a single 5-mark part (the mean M1 W1, then MW1 M1 W1 for the standard deviation) and Summer 2023 Q6(i) was 3 marks (MW1 for the mean, W1 for the sum of squares, MW1 for the answer). Most papers since 2019 also ask for two means inside the Spearman question, and in other years the grouped form of the same calculation opens the paper. The command word is Calculate, often with 'You must show your working'. Answers are given to 2 decimal places unless the question says otherwise.
traps: Adding the values and squaring the total instead of squaring each value and adding (Summer 2019 Q3; the grouped form, the fx column squared, Summer 2019 Q1 and Summer 2024 Q1)
Stopping at the mean: about 30% earned only the mean's mark (Summer 2023 Q6)
Treating a table of days as grouped data, numbering the days, or dividing the sum of squares by the sum of the values (Summer 2025 Q2)
Giving the variance where the standard deviation was asked for, so the square root is missing

steps.decision: Count the values and add them. On a plain list every value counts once, so the sheet's $\sum f$ is just $n$.
The mean comes first because the standard-deviation formula needs it. Keep it exact; rounding here moves every later figure.
Square every value first, then add. This is a different number from $\left(\sum x\right)^{2}$, and mixing the two is the single most common way this question is lost.

options: $\sum x^{2}$ means square each value and then add, so it is 13614
$\sum x^{2}$ means add the values and then square, so it is 79524
$\sum x^{2}$ means square the mean, so it is 2209
whyMenu.explain: The sigma sits outside the square, so the squaring happens inside, value by value. Adding first and squaring gives 79524, which is far too large.

steps.decision: Substitute into the sheet's formula. The value under the root is the variance; it is never negative, so a negative here means the two squares have been swapped.
Take the square root last, and give it to 2 decimal places as the paper's front page asks. The variance 60 is not the answer.

options.feedback: Yes: $16 \div 3$. That division is the first line of every question in this topic.

items.stem: Before the lesson: what does the symbol $\sum$ tell you to do?
items.skill: Reading sigma notation (new here, so a guess is fine)

options.text: Add up everything that follows it
options.feedback: Yes. $\sum x$ is add the values; $\sum x^{2}$ is add the squares.

options.text: Square everything that follows it
options.feedback: Not quite: the squaring is written separately. $\sum$ only ever means add.

options.text: Take the average of everything that follows it
options.feedback: Averaging is the division that comes after. $\sum$ is the adding on its own.

items.stem: Before the lesson: two hockey teams have both scored a mean of 3 goals a match. What else would you want to know to compare them?
items.skill: Why an average is not the whole story (nothing to revise, just a thought)

options.text: How spread out their scores are from match to match
options.feedback: Exactly the question this topic answers, and the standard deviation is the number that answers it.

options.text: Nothing more: equal means make the teams equal
options.feedback: One team may score 3 every week and the other 0 then 6. The mean hides that; the spread shows it.

options.text: Which team has more players
options.feedback: That does not change the scores. What separates the teams is how far their scores sit from the mean.

items.stem: For the values 3, 5, 8, what is $\sum x^{2}$?
items.skill: Square each value first, then add

options.feedback: That is $\left(\sum x\right)^{2}$: adding to 16 and then squaring. The sigma sits outside the square, so square first.
That is $\sum x$, with no squaring at all. The formula needs a second column of squares.

items.stem: A calculator in statistics mode shows both $\sigma_{x}$ and $s_{x}$. Which one does this specification's formula give?
items.skill: Choosing the divisor n rather than n minus 1

options.text: $\sigma_{x}$, because the formula divides by $n$
options.feedback: Yes. The sheet's formula has $\sum f$ underneath, which for a list of values is $n$.

options.text: $s_{x}$, because it is the more accurate one
options.feedback: $s_{x}$ divides by $n - 1$. It is a different quantity, and it is not what the sheet's formula produces.

options.text: Either: they always agree
options.feedback: They differ, and on a small data set they differ enough to lose the accuracy mark. Check which key you pressed.

items.stem: A pupil works out $\dfrac{\sum x^{2}}{n} - \bar{x}^{2} = 4$ for a set of values. What is the standard deviation?
items.skill: Taking the square root as the final step

options.feedback: Yes. The bracket is the variance; the standard deviation is $\sqrt{4} = 2$.
That is the variance, the number under the root. The formula finishes with a square root.
Squaring goes the wrong way. Rooting undoes the squaring that built the variance.

items.stem: A table lists five days of the week with the number of parcels delivered on each. Which is true?

prompts.prompt: The standard deviation of a list of values, in terms of $\sum x^{2}$, $n$ and $\bar{x}$.
What is the difference between $\sum x^{2}$ and $\left(\sum x\right)^{2}$?
prompts.answer: $\sum x^{2}$ squares every value and then adds the squares. $\left(\sum x\right)^{2}$ adds the values and squares the total, which is much larger and is not what the formula wants.

prompts.prompt: The four steps for the standard deviation of a list.
prompts.answer: 1 Add the values to get $\sum x$ and divide by $n$ for the mean. 2 Square each value and add to get $\sum x^{2}$. 3 Work out $\dfrac{\sum x^{2}}{n} - \bar{x}^{2}$. 4 Take the square root and round to 2 decimal places.

prompts.prompt: Why does the standard deviation carry the same units as the data, while the variance does not?
prompts.answer: The variance is built from squared differences, so its units are squared. The square root at the end brings it back to the units of the original values.

prompts.prompt: A calculator offers $\sigma_{x}$ and $s_{x}$. Which does this specification want, and why?
prompts.answer: $\sigma_{x}$. The formula on the sheet divides by $\sum f$, which for a list of values is $n$; $s_{x}$ divides by $n - 1$ and gives a different number.

prompts.prompt: What does $\sum x^{2}$ tell you to do?
prompts.answer: Square each value, then add the squares.

prompts.prompt: What is the variance, compared with the standard deviation?
prompts.answer: The standard deviation squared: the value under the root.

prompts.prompt: Which calculator value is this specification's standard deviation?

insight.ruleToRemember: Mean = sum fx / sum f; SD from sum f x squared / sum f minus mean squared, then square root; check whether the table holds raw values or frequencies; keep full precision until the final rounding.
